action.description:
Action is currently only "confirm" - auto-applies merges to every
pending pair whose confidence is at least MinConfidence. PRD §6
"bulk-confirm all ≥ 0.95 confidence" workflow.

dryRun.description:
DryRun previews the operation: returns the pairs that WOULD be
confirmed (and the excluded count) without writing anything. The UI
shows this before letting the reviewer pull the trigger.

includeEntangled.description:
IncludeEntangled opts pairs that touch OTHER pending pairs into the bulk
confirm. Default false, for the same reason type conflicts are excluded:
merging an entangled pair rewrites the question every incident pair was
asking (they get re-pointed onto the merge target), so a one-click bulk
run would silently reshape decisions the reviewer never looked at. The
single-pair dialog surfaces this as "in N other pairs"; bulk has no such
moment, so it opts out by default.

includeTypeConflicts.description:
IncludeTypeConflicts opts type-mismatch pairs into the bulk confirm.
Default false: the resolver stamps same-name/different-type collisions
at confidence 1.0 (name-certainty, not merge-certainty), so a naive
">= 0.95" would silently hard-merge every cross-type collision in the
queue. Those pairs need individual review unless explicitly included.

entity should carry — type adjudication for cross-type collisions. The

DedupByName runs a tiered duplicate-entity pass after the type mappings:

different-type collisions are routed to Entity Resolution Review as pending SAME_AS pairs.
Typically paired with property-keyed type-canonicalization mappings so the

entity-type label (surface → type, N:1) — e.g. "doctor" → "Provider",

derivation consume this direction. Legacy type → surface rows are flipped

transformed per the workspace's PII action (hash/redact/store-as-is) at

targetName and targetType).

delete.description:
Delete a conversation and everything it owns: its messages, observations, reflections, agent steps and the tool calls recorded against those steps. Entities extracted from the conversation are kept; only their links to the deleted nodes are removed.

With `purge=extracted`, the same transaction also removes what was extracted only from this conversation, and the response reports how many entities, relationships and aliases it removed:

- Entities whose every extraction source is in this conversation, together with their aliases. An entity is kept when it was created through the API or MCP, when another entity was merged into it, or when it has a relationship that the purge does not remove.
- Relationships between entities whose every source message is in this conversation, unless they were created through the API or MCP.

Relationships that survive stop listing this conversation's messages among their sources. Extracted data is identified through the messages it came from, so the purge must be requested on the delete that removes them: once a conversation has been deleted without it, its extracted data can no longer be told apart. A purge can wait briefly for an extraction running in the same workspace, so that extraction cannot attach a new mention to an entity the purge is removing. Any other `purge` value is rejected with 400 and deletes nothing.

The delete is idempotent and returns 200 even when the conversation does not exist. Repeating it for a conversation that is already gone still removes any messages, observations, reflections, agent steps and tool calls left behind under that conversation ID.

delete.description:

When a user holds more than one call can remove in time, the response has `status: "incomplete"` and the counts removed so far; repeat the call until `status` is `deleted`. The call is idempotent: once it has completed, repeating it removes nothing and returns zero counts. Repeating it also removes what an extraction already running for one of the user's messages wrote after the call returned.

While the workspace's existing memory is still being assigned to users, the call answers 503 `user_partition_not_ready` with a `Retry-After` header and deletes nothing. `userId` scopes data for a trusted backend and is not an access-control boundary. post.description: Create a typed, directed relationship between two entities. The type is validated against the workspace's relation allowlist, which includes every relationship type the active ontology declares: unknown types are written as the fallback type (RELATED_TO) with the original name preserved in the predicate field — never silently. When the ontology declares the type, its declared source/target entity types are enforced: an endpoint pair the ontology does not cover returns 422 ontology_violation under a strict ontology (the body lists the pairs it does declare) and collapses to the fallback type otherwise; when the endpoints fit, the edge is stored under the ontology's own spelling (depends_on is stored as DEPENDS_ON). Types the ontology does not declare are judged by the workspace's stored allowed_types alone and never rejected on this ground. The extraction pipeline is stricter by design: there a relation that fits no declaration is dropped, while an API call is told its write did not land. confidence defaults to 1.0. properties values must be scalars or arrays of scalars, and the server-owned keys (id, confidence, method, predicate, firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt) are rejected. The write is idempotent per (source, type, target): re-asserting an existing relationship updates lastSeenAt, averages confidence, and re-applies properties. Both entities must belong to the same user's memory (or both be shared), and to userId's when it is given; otherwise 422 cross_user_relationship. userId scopes data for a trusted backend and is not an access-control boundary. Every relationship carries a UUID id, which a re-assert returns unchanged and GET /v1/entities/{id} reports for the relationship from both ends. Requires the entities:write scope.

Idempotent: a workspace whose database already answers returns at once, and a call cut short (client timeout, disconnect) is completed by the next one, which reuses the work already done.
To bring back a database deleted for inactivity, name one of GET /v1/workspace/archives in restoreFromArchive. The call then answers status "restoring": the new database is filled from the snapshot in the background, writes are refused with 503 writes_paused until it finishes, and GET /v1/workspace reports "active" (or "error" with a statusMessage) when it does. A call without a body on a workspace with a restore that has not started cancels it. Requires a user token or Admin key whose workspace role is owner or admin.

200.description: status is active, or restoring when a snapshot is being loaded

202.description: status is provisioning and retry is true: call again

409.description: external_database, copy_in_progress (a restore is already running), or restore_not_allowed (the workspace has a database)

503.description: provisioning_failed (retry), no_capacity, or managed_provisioning_disabled

get.description: Return the workspace's typed-relation allowlist configuration, falling back to system defaults when unset, plus what the workspace's active ontology contributes. allowed_types is what the workspace stored and the only field PUT writes; ontology_types is what the active ontology declares, derived on every read; effective_allowed_types is their union and the set a relationship write is judged against. A type outside it collapses onto fallback_type, with the original name kept in the edge's predicate property. ontology_types is omitted when the workspace has no active ontology or the lookup failed.

put.description: Set the workspace's typed-relation allowlist. The body is merged on top of the system defaults, so a partial body is safe. Entries in allowed_types are case-insensitive and normalized to UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; entries containing characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_-/.,] are dropped at validation. Types declared by the workspace's active ontology are added automatically at read time and should not be listed here: sending them stores a snapshot that stops tracking the ontology once it is edited. Requires a user token whose workspace role is owner or admin — an API key is rejected with 403 user token required, even one carrying workspace:admin.

200.description: The stored config plus the resulting effective allowlist

403.description: Requires a user token with the owner or admin workspace role

post.description: Bring back a workspace whose database failed or was deleted after the inactivity window. Identical to POST /v1/workspace/provision: synchronous, idempotent, and a workspace whose database still answers is left as it is. Requires a user token or Admin key whose workspace role is owner or admin.

202.description: status is provisioning and retry is true: call again

409.description: external_database

503.description: provisioning_failed (retry), no_capacity, or managed_provisioning_disabled

get.description: Return the workspace's entity-resolution configuration, falling back to system defaults when unset.

put.description: Set the workspace's entity-resolution thresholds. The body is merged on top of the system defaults, so a partial body is safe. Validation auto-corrects pathological combinations: a review_threshold above auto_merge_threshold resets both to defaults rather than storing a band that can never be entered, and embedding_weight and fuzzy_weight are renormalized to sum to 1. Requires a user token whose workspace role is owner or admin — an API key is rejected with 403 user token required, even one carrying workspace:admin.

post.description: Create a new workspace with status "pending". A managed workspace has no database until POST /v1/workspace/provision, which callers chain straight after this one. Workspace names are unique per owner.

503.description: workspace_limit_unavailable: the managed-workspace limit could not be checked; retry
